title: Parable of the Polygons
description: Nicky Case and Vi Hart's playable post on the shape of society: how a small individual preference for neighbors like yourself compounds into a segregated system, and why it does not undo itself when the bias stops.
content:
## Parable of the Polygons

A playable post on the shape of society, by Vi Hart and Nicky Case.

[Play it at ncase.me/polygons](https://ncase.me/polygons/) — about twenty minutes.

The course draws three lessons from it (Module 7 opens with them):

1. **Small individual bias produces large collective bias.** Naming a culture's failure is not an attack on its individuals.
2. **The past haunts the present.** A floor does not stop being dirty because you stopped dropping food; creating equity is ongoing work.
3. **Demand diversity near you.** If everyone around you is a triangle, you are missing some amazing squares — and that is unfair to everyone.

Pair it with Module 4's lab, *The Evolution of Trust*, by the same author: they are two halves of one lesson about how the rules of a game shape its players.
